headline: RECORD $319M IN A SINGLE QUARTER: Discovery Mining DSV Doubles Revenue YoY, 67K oz Gold, Kidd Copper-Zinc Added — $608M Liquidity, Zero Debt
snippet: Discovery Mining (TSX: DSV) reported August 13 its highest-ever quarterly revenue at $319.1 million — more than double Q2 2025 and 12% above Q1 2026 — driven by record gold output of 67,309 oz (up 33% year over year) and an average realized gold price near $4,400. Net earnings hit $52.1 million ($0.06/share), adjusted EBITDA was $170 million, and the company ended the period with $607.8 million in total liquidity and no debt, having completed the June 1 acquisition of Kidd Operations (copper and zinc). For investors tracking the lag between gold's price performance and miner earnings delivery: Discovery's Q2 print is the starkest single-company illustration yet of what $4,300-plus gold does to producer free cash flow at current cost structures — the operating leverage is now fully visible in reported numbers, not just in forecast models.

headline: SWEDEN CLEARS BOLIDEN'S LAVER: Appeals Rejected — New Copper Mine Could DOUBLE Sweden's Output, Add 10% to EU Supply
snippet: Sweden's government rejected both appeals against Boliden's mining concession for the Laver copper project on August 12, clearing a significant hurdle for a deposit whose extraction could double Sweden's copper production and expand total EU output by approximately 10%. The concession — originally granted by Sweden's Chief Mining Inspector in September 2025 — can now progress toward the Land and Environment Court environmental permitting phase, though Boliden still faces approvals related to winter grazing land used by the Semisjaur-Njarg Sámi reindeer herding community. For European copper supply chain context: Laver sits within Boliden's existing operational footprint in northern Sweden and, if permitted, would represent one of the largest new copper development projects in the EU at a time when the bloc is actively legislating domestic critical minerals production targets under the Critical Raw Materials Act.

headline: PHILIPPINES' RICHEST COPPER-GOLD MINE JOINS NATION'S BIGGEST MINER: SM Investments Folds Tampakan Into Dominion — 375,000 Tonnes Cu Per Year
snippet: SM Investments Corp. — controlled by the family of the late billionaire Henry Sy — announced August 12-13 that it will transfer its 34% stake in Atlas Consolidated Mining to Dominion Holdings and fold in the Tampakan copper-gold project, creating what would be the Philippines' largest listed mining company. Tampakan, located in southern Mindanao, is projected to produce an average of 375,000 tonnes of copper and 360,000 ounces of gold in concentrate annually over a 17-year mine life once it starts production in 2028 — two years later than originally targeted. The Dominion consolidation is the largest domestic Philippine mining restructuring since the country's 2021 mining moratorium ended, and the combined entity's copper production timeline aligns precisely with the decade when analysts project Southeast Asia's grid electrification program will require the most copper per dollar of GDP growth.

headline: $160 BILLION REBORN: Bougainville Clears Lloyds Metals to Restart Panguna — 5.3Mt Copper, 19.3Moz Gold Dormant Since 1989 Civil War
snippet: The Autonomous Bougainville Government granted Lloyds Metals & Energy Ltd. permission on August 7-12, 2026 to carry out feasibility activities and preparatory works to assess the redevelopment of Panguna — the giant copper-gold mine in Papua New Guinea that was shuttered in 1989 after environmental protests escalated into a civil conflict that killed up to 20,000 people. Panguna's remaining reserves are estimated at 5.3 million tonnes of copper and 19.3 million ounces of gold, worth approximately $160 billion at current prices. The government stressed that construction and production are not yet permitted; 'redevelopment will proceed one step at a time.' Panguna's re-opening would represent one of the largest additions to the global copper supply pipeline at a moment when copper's structural deficit is projected to widen through 2030.

headline: STALLION URANIUM STUD HITS HIGHEST RADIOACTIVITY EVER AT COYOTE — Athabasca Program Expanded to 6,750m as Results Intensify
snippet: Stallion Uranium Corp. (TSX-V: STUD) announced August 13 that drilling at its Coyote target in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin has intersected the highest radioactivity encountered to date in the program, prompting management to expand the drill program from 5,500 metres to 6,750 metres — a 23% increase — with 4,626 metres (84% of the original program) already completed across drill holes ML26-005 and ML26-006A. At uranium spot now holding above $87/lb — up nearly 20% year over year — any Athabasca Basin program that delivers escalating radioactivity readings is being watched closely: the Basin hosts the world's highest-grade uranium deposits, and a discovery in the Coyote structural corridor would immediately draw comparisons to nearby historical high-grade deposits that served as the Basin's defining exploration templates.

headline: NEXGOLD HOLDS $101M CASH AS GOLDBORO FEASIBILITY STUDY NEARS COMPLETION: NEXG Expands Drill Program 33% to 40,000m on Positive Results
snippet: NexGold Mining Corp. (TSX-V: NEXG) reported August 13 its Q2 2026 financial results, ending the period with $101.1 million in cash against a net loss of $16.0 million ($0.06/share) as the company remains pre-production. The headline operational development: an infill reverse circulation drill program at Goldboro returned results strong enough that management expanded the planned program from 30,000 metres to 40,000 metres mid-campaign, with the updated Goldboro Feasibility Study now on track for completion in 2026. A feasibility study delivery at current gold prices — with Goldboro located in Nova Scotia and subject to Canadian permitting rather than jurisdictional risk — positions NexGold as one of the clearest near-term development catalysts in the Atlantic Canada gold space if the FS numbers reflect the grade continuity the expanded drill program is targeting.

headline: 27 METRES OF 1.89% Li2O AT ROSE WEST: Critical Elements CRE Resumes 10,000m Quebec Lithium Program — Grades Hold Into Expansion Zone
source_name: StreetInsider / Critical Elements Lithium Corp. (TSX-V: CRE)
snippet: Critical Elements Lithium Corporation (TSX-V: CRE) released August 12 Phase 2 Summer 2026 assay results from its Rose West Discovery in Eeyou Istchee, Québec, reporting 27.35 metres grading 1.89% Li2O and 161 ppm Ta2O5 — including a 10.50-metre high-grade core at 2.70% Li2O and 222 ppm Ta2O5 — confirming that lithium and tantalum grades remain consistent as systematic 100-metre grid drilling expands the known pegmatite boundary toward a potential 1,250 x 2,000 metre mineralised footprint. With eleven holes totalling 2,073 metres drilled in the northeast main target area, Rose West is progressing on the geometry pattern — grade-consistent expansion at each successive step-out — that most commonly precedes a material resource estimate upward revision in Quebec spodumene-hosted lithium pegmatites.

headline: COBRASCO KEEPS GROWING DEEPER: Andina Copper ANDC Drills 264m @ 0.63% Cu From 36m — Porphyry Mineralization Confirmed to 844m Depth in Colombia
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Andina Copper Corp. (TSX-V: ANDC)
snippet: Andina Copper Corporation (TSX-V: ANDC) announced August 11 that drill hole CDH010 at its Cobrasco Porphyry Copper-Moly Discovery in Chocó, Colombia returned 264 metres grading 0.63% Cu and 35 ppm Mo from 36 metres depth within a broader intercept of 504 metres at 0.48% Cu — extending porphyry-style mineralization continuously from near-surface to the final drill depth of 844.65 metres. The result confirms that the Cobrasco system remains open at depth, with the near-surface shallow start (36m) and continuous grade to 844m defining a geometry profile that in Andean porphyry deposits typically indicates a much larger system than the current drill fence alone can bound. At copper above $6.50/lb, a Colombian porphyry copper discovery with this scale indicator and shallow, drill-accessible geometry is exactly the type of project that receives major-company partnership interest ahead of a defined resource.

headline: GOLDEN GATE BREAKS 320m NORTHEAST: Goliath GOT Intercepts 10.32 g/t Au Over 6m at BC's Surebet — Visible Gold Now in 25 of 45 Holes
snippet: Goliath Resources Limited (TSX-V: GOT) reported August 11 assay results confirming the northeastward expansion of the Golden Gate Zone by 320 metres within the 100%-owned Golddigger Property in BC's Golden Triangle, with the best new result returning 10.32 g/t gold over 6.00 metres in the expansion area — including 65.65 g/t gold over 0.75 metres in a visible-gold intercept. The 2026 drill campaign has now identified macroscopic visible gold in 25 of 45 holes completed, a strike rate that for high-grade vein-hosted gold deposits in the Golden Triangle is among the highest in the camp's recent exploration history. Each new zone extension confirmed at Surebet adds to the argument that this is a large-scale, structurally-controlled system rather than a small bonanza pocket — the distinction that separates a multi-million-ounce discovery from a curiosity in BC's most productive gold terrain.

headline: GREENLAND PUNCHES TWO TICKETS: Amaroq AMRQ Posts C$37M Q2 From 22 g/t Nalunaq Gold While REE Drilling Begins at Ilua Pegmatite
snippet: Amaroq Minerals Ltd. (AIM: AMRQ) reported August 13 its Q2 2026 results showing C$37.3 million in revenue from the Nalunaq underground gold mine in Greenland — which is processing ore at a head grade of 22.2 g/t gold with recoveries now at 90% following successful flotation circuit commissioning — while simultaneously announcing that 699 metres of first-ever drilling has been completed at the Ilua Pegmatite rare earth element prospect within the Nunarsuit Joint Venture licence area in South Greenland, with initial REE drill results expected before year-end. Greenland's rare earth pegmatite geology, combined with the island's accelerating political integration into NATO supply-chain diplomacy following the 2025 US-Denmark framework agreement, positions any confirmed Ilua REE discovery as a strategically significant Western supply asset at a moment when China's export restrictions on heavy rare earths are reshaping procurement strategy across the defence and EV sectors.
